Product change: workspace ownership can be handed over, with the new owner's consent.

Every workspace has exactly one recorded owner — the member Taskflow treats as *the* owner: the person who is alerted when someone new joins, and the one billing belongs to. Today that is fixed when the workspace is created. From now on the recorded owner can offer the workspace to another member, who takes it over by accepting.

User stories

- As the workspace owner, I can offer my workspace to any other active member. The offered member gets a notification of a new kind, `ownership_handover`, inviting them to accept; nobody else is alerted. Only one offer can be open per workspace: while one is open, a further offer is refused until the open one is withdrawn, declined or lapsed. An offer lapses exactly seven days after it was made: an offer made at instant T can still be acted on before T + 7 days, and no longer from T + 7 days on.
- As the offered member, I can accept — whatever my current role. When I accept, I become the recorded owner and hold the owner role, and the previous owner steps down to admin (if they still hold the owner role at that moment). If I already held the owner role, only the previous owner's role changes. The workspace has an owner at every instant during the handover; the existing rule that a workspace never loses its last owner must not get in the way. I can instead decline, after which nothing is pending and the owner may offer again.
- As the owner who made an offer, I can withdraw it while it is open.
- As any member of the workspace, I can see whether an offer is open and to whom.

Consequences of acceptance (all of these must hold)

- Every role change made by the handover is announced exactly as a manual role change is (the `member.role_changed` event, carrying the member, the role before and the role after), and the handover itself publishes a new domain event `organization.ownership_transferred` (`EventEnvelope & { fromUserId: UserId; toUserId: UserId }`, added to `TaskflowEventMap`), which the audit log records as an `organization.ownership_transferred` action on the organization (subject kind `organization`, subject id the workspace's, metadata `{ fromUserId, toUserId }`). Everything published during acceptance is on behalf of the accepting member.
- Everything that follows "the owner" follows the new one: alerts about new members go to the new owner and no longer to the previous one; managing billing (for example changing the plan) is now the new owner's and is refused to the previous owner; and the previous owner, now an admin, can be removed from the workspace like any other admin.

Guards and refusals

- Only the recorded owner may offer or withdraw. Holding the owner role is not enough: a second member who has been given the owner role but is not the recorded owner is refused. Both refusals are a `PermissionDeniedError`.
- An offer must go to an active member of the same workspace other than the owner. An unknown user, a user from another workspace or a removed member → `NotFoundError` (the one in `src/server/services/_support.ts`). The owner themselves → the refusal `"self"`.
- Only the offered member can accept or decline. Anyone else acting on the offer gets the refusal `"nothing_pending"`, and so does everyone when no offer is open (accepting a second time, declining after a withdrawal, withdrawing when nothing is open). Accepting or declining an offer that has lapsed → `"expired"`; a lapsed offer no longer counts as open: it is not shown, it does not block a new offer, and acting on it changes nothing.
- A new offer while one is open → `"pending_exists"`.
- These refusals throw a new `OwnershipHandoverError`, exported from `src/lib/errors.ts`: it extends `Error`, has `readonly code = "conflict"` and `readonly reason: OwnershipHandoverRefusal`, where `export type OwnershipHandoverRefusal = "self" | "pending_exists" | "nothing_pending" | "expired"`. `toAppError` maps it to the `conflict` code and `isDomainError` recognises it.
- An `orgId` outside the actor's workspace → `TenantScopeError`, on every operation. An offer in one workspace is invisible from another.
- If either side leaves the workspace while the offer is open — the offered member is removed, or the offering owner is removed (possible when the workspace has another member with the owner role) — the offer is withdrawn automatically.

Offers are persisted; a freshly migrated database (the way the test suite builds one) must have whatever you add.

In `src/types/organization.ts`:

```ts
  readonly id: string;
  readonly orgId: OrgId;
  readonly fromUserId: UserId;
  readonly toUserId: UserId;
  readonly status: OwnershipHandoverStatus;
  readonly expiresAt: IsoTimestamp;
  readonly createdAt: IsoTimestamp;
  readonly resolvedAt: IsoTimestamp | null;
}
```

`expiresAt` is exactly seven days after `createdAt`. An open offer has status `"pending"` and no `resolvedAt`; an offer that was accepted, declined or withdrawn carries that status and the instant it was resolved.

- `export async function cancelOwnershipHandover(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId): Promise<OwnershipHandover>` — the withdrawal.
- `export async function getPendingOwnershipHandover(actor: Actor, orgId: OrgId): Promise<OwnershipHandover | null>` — the open offer, or `null`.

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

18	/**
19	 * A removed member is archived, never deleted, and no read ever surfaces one:
20	 * the scope is fixed here rather than threaded through every call site.
21	 */
22	const LIVE_MEMBERS: { readonly includeArchived?: boolean } = {};

24	function liveMemberPredicate() {
25	  return shouldFilterArchived(LIVE_MEMBERS) ? isNull(members.archivedAt) : undefined;
26	}

28	export async function findMember(
29	  orgId: OrgId,
30	  userId: UserId,
31	): Promise<Member | null> {
32	  const row = getDb()
33	    .select()
34	    .from(members)
35	    .where(
36	      and(
37	        orgPredicate(members.orgId, orgId),
38	        eq(members.userId, userId),
39	        liveMemberPredicate(),
40	      ),
41	    )
42	    .get();
43	  return row ? toMember(row) : null;
44	}

47	  orgId: OrgId,
48	  memberId: MemberId,
49	): Promise<Member | null> {
50	  const row = getDb()
51	    .select()
52	    .from(members)
53	    .where(and(orgPredicate(members.orgId, orgId), eq(members.id, memberId)))
54	    .get();

56	}

58	/** Cursor-paged member list joined with the user record the UI renders. */
59	export async function listMembers(
60	  input: ListMembersInput,
61	): Promise<Page<MemberWithUser>> {
62	  const db = getDb();
63	  const sort = { sortColumn: members.createdAt, idColumn: members.id };
64	
65	  const filters = compact(
66	    orgPredicate(members.orgId, input.orgId),
67	    liveMemberPredicate(),
68	    input.role === undefined ? undefined : eq(members.role, input.role),
69	    input.status === undefined ? undefined : eq(members.status, input.status),
70	    input.query === undefined
71	      ? undefined
72	      : or(
73	          like(users.name, `%${input.query}%`),
74	          like(users.email, `%${input.query}%`),
75	        ),
76	  );
77	
78	  const total = db
79	    .select({ value: count() })
80	    .from(members)
81	    .innerJoin(users, eq(users.id, members.userId))
82	    .where(and(...filters))
83	    .get();
84	
85	  const rows = db
86	    .select({ member: members, user: users })
87	    .from(members)
88	    .innerJoin(users, eq(users.id, members.userId))
89	    .where(and(...filters, ...compact(keysetPredicate(sort, input.cursor))))
90	    .orderBy(desc(members.createdAt), desc(members.id))
91	    .limit(probeLimit(input.limit))
92	    .all();
93	
94	  return toPage(
95	    rows,
96	    input.limit,
97	    total?.value ?? 0,
98	    (row) => ({ ...toMember(row.member), user: toUser(row.user) }),
99	    (row) => ({ id: row.member.id, sortValue: row.member.createdAt }),
100	  );
101	}

107	    .from(members)
108	    .where(
109	      and(
110	        orgPredicate(members.orgId, orgId),
111	        eq(members.status, "active"),
112	        liveMemberPredicate(),
113	      ),

152	    .update(members)

317	/**
318	 * Brings `databasePath` up to date. Generated migrations win when they exist;
319	 * otherwise the embedded schema is pushed. Safe to run repeatedly — every
320	 * statement is `IF NOT EXISTS`.
321	 */
322	export async function runMigrations(
323	  databasePath: string = process.env.TASKFLOW_DB_PATH ?? DEFAULT_DB_PATH,
324	): Promise<void> {
325	  const absolute = resolve(process.cwd(), databasePath);
326	  mkdirSync(dirname(absolute), { recursive: true });
327	
328	  const sqlite = new Database(absolute);
329	  sqlite.pragma("journal_mode = WAL");
330	
331	  try {
332	    for (const statement of readMigrationStatements()) {
333	      sqlite.exec(statement);
334	    }
335	  } finally {
336	    sqlite.close();
337	  }
338	}
339	
340	/** `pnpm db:migrate` runs this file directly; importing it must stay inert. */
341	if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith("migrate.ts") === true) {
342	  await runMigrations();
343	}
344	
345	function readMigrationStatements(): readonly string[] {
346	  const dir = resolve(process.cwd(), MIGRATIONS_DIR);
347	  if (!existsSync(dir)) return SCHEMA_STATEMENTS;
348	
349	  const files = readdirSync(dir)
350	    .filter((name) => name.endsWith(".sql"))
351	    .sort();
352	
353	  if (files.length === 0) return SCHEMA_STATEMENTS;
354	
355	  return files.flatMap((name) =>
356	    readFileSync(join(dir, name), "utf8")
357	      .split("--> statement-breakpoint")
358	      .map((chunk) => chunk.trim())
359	      .filter(Boolean),
360	  );
361	}

/**
 * Brings `databasePath` up to date. Generated migrations win when they exist;
 * otherwise the embedded schema is pushed. Safe to run repeatedly — every
 * statement is `IF NOT EXISTS`.
 */
export async function runMigrations(
  databasePath: string = process.env.TASKFLOW_DB_PATH ?? DEFAULT_DB_PATH,
): Promise<void> {
  const absolute = resolve(process.cwd(), databasePath);
  mkdirSync(dirname(absolute), { recursive: true });

  const sqlite = new Database(absolute);
  sqlite.pragma("journal_mode = WAL");

  try {
    for (const statement of readMigrationStatements()) {
      sqlite.exec(statement);
    }
  } finally {
    sqlite.close();
  }
}

/** `pnpm db:migrate` runs this file directly; importing it must stay inert. */
if (process.argv[1]?.endsWith("migrate.ts") === true) {
  await runMigrations();
}

function readMigrationStatements(): readonly string[] {
  const dir = resolve(process.cwd(), MIGRATIONS_DIR);
  if (!existsSync(dir)) return SCHEMA_STATEMENTS;

  const files = readdirSync(dir)
    .filter((name) => name.endsWith(".sql"))
    .sort();

  if (files.length === 0) return SCHEMA_STATEMENTS;

  return files.flatMap((name) =>
    readFileSync(join(dir, name), "utf8")
      .split("--> statement-breakpoint")
      .map((chunk) => chunk.trim())
      .filter(Boolean),
  );
}
